articles.title: The Milburn report forgets what social security is for
articles.summary: Alan Milburn’s report on young people not in education, employment, or training aims to get more young people less dependent on “welfare” and help them move into employment. But Ruth Patrick argues, this is an old policy proposal of cuts to social security with a better communications approach. At heart such policies forget what social … Continued The post The Milburn report forgets what social security is for first appeared on LSE British Politics .

articles.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a time $t_{c}$ of calculation in an $N$ qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time $t_H$, $t_c\ll t_H$, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale $\tau_r$. If $t_H\gg t_c >\sim \tau_r$ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since $t_H$ scales exponentially with $N$ there is a threshold $N_c$ such that for $N\gg N_c$ one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find $N_c\approx \ln(\tau_r/T)$ where $T$ is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. $\tau_r$ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.

articles.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.

articles.title: QEDist: Practical Exact Distance Certification for Stabilizer Codes
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21709v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present QEDist, a method and software package that certifies the distance of qubit stabilizer codes. Building on tree-search methods, QEDist constructs candidate logical operators one qubit at a time, using sparse parity checks, stabilizer equivalence, and verified symmetries to reduce the work. For a cutoff $W$, a completed search either finds a nontrivial logical operator of weight at most $W$ or proves that none exists. Because satisfying one check can violate another, we use both satisfied and unsatisfied checks to lower-bound the weight needed to complete a logical operator, and prune branches whose bound exceeds the remaining budget, which substantially reduces net search time. We benchmark QEDist mainly on Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes; the same formulation extends to non-CSS codes and to the fault distance of syndrome-extraction circuits. For lifted-product (LP) codes, we further exploit the product structure to replace part of the full-code search with a smaller search on a classical constituent. We establish exact distances for codes with up to several thousand qubits, including Abelian and non-Abelian LP codes whose distances were previously reported only as upper bounds. In several seconds of search on one laptop core, QEDist certifies exact distances up to 20 for many of these codes and fault distance 10 for the syndrome-extraction circuit of the $[[144,12,12]]$ code. With orders-of-magnitude speedups over the tested exact solvers, QEDist makes exact distance certification a practical tool for selecting an

articles.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $\Omega(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $\Theta(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.

articles.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.

articles.title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) rely on measured quantum observables to guide optimization, but hardware noise can suppress the parameter-dependent signals essential for learning. Here, we develop a structure-preserving error-mitigation framework that improves QNN trainability through reusable calibration of the quantum circuit's effective noise response. By calibrating a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit, we construct regularized estimators of local quantum features that remain fixed throughout training. We quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect the recovery of both observables and their derivatives. Numerical simulations demonstrate enhanced loss-landscape contrast, faster convergence, and improved classification performance, and an IBM Quantum experiment confirms improved closed-loop variational optimization under hardware noise. We further demonstrate calibration reuse in a modular QNN comprising 25 independent four-qubit channels, corresponding to 100 qubits in aggregate. Our results establish reusable feature calibration as a practical approach to improving noise-limited quantum machine learning without repeated calibration at every training step.

articles.title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topol

articles.title: Loss-Tolerant Quantum Correlations Between Atomic and Photonic Qubits
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum physics forbids cloning of a qubit. Therefore, a qubit is irreversibly lost upon loss of the information carrier. To mitigate this physical loss, it has been proposed to distribute the logical information across an entangled set of physical qubits, some of which can be lost. Previous experiments illustrated this concept, but failed to demonstrate a gain in the information-retrieval efficiency. Here we address this challenge with photons for which the total loss, from generation to detection, is below the loss-tolerance threshold of $50\%$. Using two single-atom emitters in an optical cavity, we encode information into the photons of a graph state and observe an efficiency gain for retrieving quantum correlations between the atoms and the photons for single-qubit measurements in the Pauli $X$ and $Z$ bases. Although technical errors reduce the probability to obtain the \textit{correct} result, we achieve average fidelities as high as $\gtrsim\!70\%$ without and $\gtrsim\!75\%$ with error detection, demonstrating entanglement between the atomic and encoded photonic qubits. Lowering the encoding errors is a next natural step toward loss-tolerant photonic quantum-information processing.

articles.title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 82 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.

articles.title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.

articles.title: Quantum Reference Frames, Locality, and Microcausality in Quantum Field Theory
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As a consequence of the relativistic spectrum condition, quantum reference frames for translations on Minkowski space are never described by projection-valued measures, and in many cases fail a weaker spacetime localisation property known as the norm-$1$ condition. This has several implications for the local and observable structure of quantum field theories described relative to even the best available frame: for a large class of frame states, strict locality is replaced by almost locality, and microcausality by commutators that decay rapidly with increasing separation, corresponding to an effective smearing of the light cone by the localisation density of the frame state. Operations built from finitely many almost local Kraus operators, for example nonselective measurements of relativised local observables, satisfy an approximate no-signalling bound, with a residue attributable to the localisation uncertainty of the frame. Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.

articles.title: Transient State Preservation of a Dissipative Qubit via Lyapunov Control
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preserving quantum states in the presence of environmental decoherence remains a fundamental challenge for quantum information processing. This work investigates whether Hamiltonian Lyapunov feedback can transiently preserve the state of an open qubit by reshaping its trajectory under Markovian dissipation. A state-error Lyapunov function is adopted to derive an analytical feedback law for Lindblad dynamics, ensuring a nonincreasing Lyapunov function whenever the control sensitivities are nonzero. The analysis identifies the geometric conditions under which the feedback becomes ineffective, showing that control authority vanishes when the current and target Bloch vectors are collinear. Numerical simulations are performed for amplitude damping and pure dephasing using selected target states. Performance is evaluated through fidelity, accumulated infidelity, dwell time above a fidelity threshold, coherence, and control effort. The results demonstrate that the proposed feedback cannot eliminate irreversible dissipation or achieve universal asymptotic stabilization, but it can provide transient benefits for selected target-channel combinations. In particular, under amplitude damping, the controller significantly reduces accumulated infidelity and substantially extends the interval during which the system remains above a prescribed fidelity threshold. In the pure dephasing cases examined, improvements in fidelity are generally limited, although transient coherence preservation is observed for the oblique target considered, revealin

articles.title: Microwave-optical quantum transduction with quantum-well exciton polaritons
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linking superconducting quantum processors over optical fiber requires microwave-optical quantum transducers that are efficient, high-bandwidth, and low-noise. This combination has been out of reach because of the weak nonlinearities of conventional electro-optic (EO) materials. We propose a transducer with an engineered, strong EO nonlinearity using the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) of quantum-well excitons. The QCSE transducer leverages the strong light-matter interactions and extreme polarizability of quantum well excitons. Strong coupling to an optical cavity forms exciton-polaritons whose vacuum EO coupling is up to five orders of magnitude larger than in a typical thin-film lithium niobate device. We describe a GaAs/AlGaAs stepped-quantum-well transducer design with predicted transduction efficiencies above 60% and fewer than 0.01 added noise quanta over a $\sim$60 MHz bandwidth, using pump powers below 10 $\mu$W and loaded optical and microwave quality factors of only $3\times10^4$ and $10^3$. We further show that the cavity protection of the polariton provides robustness against inhomogeneous broadening of the quantum well excitons.

articles.title: Charge self-consistent DFT+QDMFT framework with a Krylov-based quantum impurity solver
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We integrate a quantum impurity solver into a charge self-consistent density functional theory (DFT) plus quantum dynamical mean-field theory framework. The solver optimizes adaptive circuits to approximate the ground state of the impurity model and its particle and hole excitations, and reconstructs the impurity Green's function from their Hamiltonian moments. Higher-order moments are predicted from low-order ones using a machine-learning model, while regularized optimization mitigates violations of causality in the resulting self-energy. The latter is used to update the charge density until self-consistency is achieved. We demonstrate the framework through body-centered cubic lithium calculations and compare the results with a reference one using a continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo solver. These calculations converge with root-mean-square charge-density residuals below $\boldsymbol{2\times10^{-3}}$ and yield a nearly vanishing impurity self-energy, consistent with the noninteracting limit used for weakly correlated lithium.

articles.title: Infrared fluctuations and collective entanglement modes in harmonic lattices
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how infrared fluctuations and spatial separation shape vacuum entanglement between two finite regions in the relativistic harmonic chain and its Lifshitz generalizations. At fixed lattice spacing and finite geometry, we establish that logarithmic negativity remains uniformly bounded as the mass approaches zero, while mutual information diverges. Infrared-enhanced total correlations therefore do not provide an unbounded distillable-entanglement resource. Using local symplectic consolidation, we identify the collective canonical modes carrying the negativity and follow their evolution with separation. Their participation crosses over from localization near the facing boundaries to a collective distribution within each region. Expansion in the adjacent-state canonical basis connects this evolution to progressively weaker, more extended reference modes, including adjacent-halo directions. Building on the established concentration of long-distance logarithmic negativity into a single canonical pair, we show that its spatial participation is smooth and infrared-dominated despite its ultraviolet canonical structure, a distinction also present in pure-state entanglement modes. These results refine the ultraviolet mode picture by resolving the long-wavelength organization of the oscillators participating in the surviving entanglement. Across the massless dispersions studied, the normalized participation approaches a universal long-distance profile when separation is scaled by the negativity radius. Its detailed form and

articles.title: Quantum-Classical Separation in Probability Distribution Transport via Nonlocal Games
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many-body physics and generative artificial intelligence, locality provides a natural notion of phase equivalence: two quantum states or classical probability distributions are regarded as in the same phase when local dynamics can reversibly transform one into the other. This raises a fundamental question: can local quantum dynamics transport classical probability distributions in ways that local classical dynamics cannot? We establish a quantum-classical separation in distribution transport: two classical distributions can be connected exactly and reversibly by a constant-depth local quantum circuit, whereas classical stochastic transport requires a substantially larger spatial range. We demonstrate this separation explicitly on a one-dimensional chain and develop a general construction principle on graphs, based on nonlocal games. Moreover, the source distribution can itself be generated by a simple local classical process, establishing a quantum advantage in distribution generation as well. Our results reveal a fundamental distinction between classical and quantum local reversibility, even when both the initial and final states are entirely classical.

articles.title: Quantum Fisher information matrices for time-evolved bosonic Gaussian thermal states
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) is a fundamental quantum metrological quantity arising from the second order term in a Taylor expansion of a smooth divergence evaluated at nearby quantum states. The $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix is a QFI measure arising from the $\alpha$-$z$ R\'enyi relative entropy, and QFI measures corresponding to various underlying smooth divergences may be recovered from the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix, including the standard symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) QFI. Bosonic Gaussian states are common probe states for quantum metrological tasks and admit a complete characterization in terms of their first and second moments. In this work, we consider the quantum metrological task of estimating parameters that characterize a Gaussian unitary time evolution of a faithful bosonic Gaussian thermal state. We establish a formula for the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix of faithful bosonic Gaussian thermal states that have undergone a Gaussian unitary time evolution. As an example, we calculate entries of the $\alpha$-$z$ information matrix for a two-mode Gaussian thermal state that has undergone a beam splitting operation. For a parametrized family of time-evolved bosonic Gaussian states, we also derive a formula for the SLD operator, which is known to provide a measurement scheme that saturates the quantum Cr\'amer-Rao bound and thus achieves the ultimate precision for single parameter estimation.

articles.title: A Geometric Framework for Local-to-Global Symmetry: Global Constraints on Local Dynamics
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aggregate molecular systems are routinely understood by decomposing them into local structural units, such as monomers in J/H-aggregates, chemical moieties, motifs, and functional groups. Implicit in such decompositions is the assumption that these local structures remain meaningful within the aggregate. Here, we ask how the symmetries of constituent structures relate to aggregate symmetry, and how this relation determines the constraints that global symmetry imposes on transitions between local symmetry sectors. We construct a covariant local-to-global representation from framed local symmetry data and show that its reconstruction map intertwines with a global quantum representation. By identifying which global symmetry sectors overlap each local symmetry sector, we resolve symmetry-enforced dynamical exclusions into site-resolved pathways. Through Frobenius reciprocity, these exclusions can be determined from standard character tables of the local and global symmetry groups, with the character values in the inner product paired according to the relative positions and orientations of local structures within the aggregate. Although motivated by molecular aggregates, the construction is formulated for arbitrary geometries modeled by a homogeneous space of an ambient transformation group.

articles.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. We simulate memory experiments of bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, using trapped-ion informed noise models. Depending on the physical error rate and BB code, we find up to 3-4 orders of magnitude logical error rate reduction compared to the $\texttt{BP-LSD}$ decoder, and up to 2-3 orders of magnitude lower logical error rate compared to the $\texttt{Beamsearch}$ decoder. By leveraging available classical processing time, our decoding protocol significantly boosts decoding accuracy, ultimately reducing the demands on increasing code size.

articles.title: Simplifying models of noisy stabilizer QEC on leakage qubits by Pauli twirling
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing capabilities of quantum error-correction (QEC) experiments make it increasingly important to develop methods that predict or assess logical performance over many QEC cycles. Prior work has shown that a stabilizer QEC cycle subject to Pauli-stochastic noise can be modeled by a classical Markov process over syndrome states, with a logical Pauli channel attached to each syndrome transition. Here, we extend this framework to systems in which physical qubits are subject to leakage. We first develop the theory of leakage-dephased Pauli twirling and show that twirled processes can be expressed in terms of Pauli maps on the computational subspace, conditioned on transitions between leakage patterns. We apply this theory to noisy stabilizer QEC with leakage, demonstrating that a QEC cycle with leakage can be modeled by a classical Markov process over the joint syndrome and leakage patterns, with a logical Pauli channel attached to each joint transition. Finally, we derive a transfer-matrix description of repeated QEC cycles and an exact transfer-matrix expression for the success probability of a QEC memory experiment. This framework connects leaky error models of the individual components of the QEC cycle to many-cycle logical performance and provides a foundation for logical characterization and benchmarking methods that can account for leakage.

articles.title: Perceptual glimpses are locally accumulated and globally maintained at distinct processing levels
articles.summary: Making decisions often requires the integration of multiple pieces of information. An extensive body of research has investigated the neural architecture underpinning evidence accumulation in perceptual tasks where information is continuously present, but less is known about how this neural architecture operates in situations affording only intermittent glimpses of an evidence source. In two electroencephalography experiments, human participants judged the direction of up to two pulses of motion evidence separated by gaps of varying duration. Our behavioural analysis found that participants used both pulses but underutilised the second and showed no systematic decrease in accuracy as a function of gap duration. At the neural level, motor beta lateralisation tracked cumulative evidence across pulses, maintaining a sustained representation of the decision variable through the gap and until response. In contrast, the centroparietal positivity (CPP), a previously characterised signature of evidence accumulation, built up transiently to a peak that scaled with each pulse’s contribution to the decision variable (i.e. the absolute belief update it produced), falling back to baseline in between pulses. These patterns were recapitulated in a model where pulse-information transiently integrated at the CPP level is fed to and maintained at a bounded motor level. In this model, the evidence in the second pulse is only integrated to the extent that the evidence in the first pulse falls short of the bound, or not integrated at all if a bound has already been hit.

articles.title: Human mitochondrial DNA variants influence telomere length
articles.summary: Telomere shortening is a hallmark of aging, yet telomere length (TL) varies considerably between individuals and is strongly influenced by inheritance. In mice, efficient mitochondrial function and low reactive oxygen species (ROS) production are essential for telomere elongation during early embryogenesis. As mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) encodes several subunits of the electron transport chain, we investigated whether mtDNA variants influence TL using a transmitochondrial cybrid model. Platelet-derived mitochondria from human donors with varying TL were introduced into mtDNA-depleted cells. Donor blood TL inversely correlated with cybrid ROS levels, suggesting that specific mtDNA variants may support telomere maintenance by enhancing mitochondrial fitness. During cybrid formation, a transient oxidative stress phase precedes cellular adaptation. At this stage, mtDNA variants associated with reduced complex I (CI) activity triggered rapid telomere shortening, which was rescued by antioxidant and NAD<sup>+</sup> precursor supplementation. Although these variants occur naturally in some individuals with long telomeres, our findings suggest that, under conditions of acute in vitro oxidative stress, CI activity is critical for preserving telomere integrity, potentially through the regulation of NAD<sup>+</sup>/NADH balance and PARP1 activity. Overall, our findings support a role for mtDNA variation in human TL regulation and highlight potential therapeutic opportunities involving mitochondrial replacement strategies.

articles.title: Correction: Uncovering the electrical synapse proteome in retinal neurons via in vivo proximity labeling
A Gαq/11-IP<sub>3</sub>R1-ANO1 pacemaking axis underlies pressure-induced lymphatic chronotropy
articles.summary: The frequency of spontaneous lymphatic contractions is exquisitely sensitive to changes in intraluminal pressure, enabling lymph transport to be matched to the filling state of the lymphatic capillary network. The mechanistic basis of this mechanosensitive response was investigated using ex vivo contraction assays of mouse popliteal collecting vessels. Based on electrophysiological and transcriptional similarities between lymphatic muscle cells (LMCs) and arterial smooth muscle, we hypothesized that pressure-dependent chronotropy shares a parallel signaling process with pressure-induced arterial depolarization/constriction. Thus, we probed two potential mechanisms: (1) pressure-induced activation of mechanosensitive cation channels and (2) mechano-activation of GNAQ/GNA11-coupled G-protein receptors (GPCRs) that would generate second messengers to activate those channels. Contraction assays were combined with scRNA-seq analysis of the respective targets and use of transgenic mice. Our findings rule out significant roles for the mechanosensitive channels implicated in arterial myogenic constriction, as well as channels implicated in ionic pacemaking of other tissues. In contrast, smooth-muscle specific knock out or inhibition of ANO1, IP<sub>3</sub>R1, or GNAQ/GNA11 significantly abrogated pressure-induced chronotropy. These results support a scheme whereby mechano-activation of one or more GNAQ/GNA11-coupled GPCRs generates IP<sub>3</sub>, inducing sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca<sup>2+</sup> release through IP<sub>3</sub>R1, which drives depolarization through the activation of

articles.title: Rhodopsin 7 is an ancestral non-canonical photoreceptor that shapes light-responsive behavior
articles.summary: Animals rely on light not only for vision but also to adapt behavior to their environment through non-image-forming pathways. In Drosophila, most rhodopsins mediate retinal image formation, but Rhodopsin 7 (RH7) is widely expressed in the brain and optic lobe, acting as a non-canonical light sensor reminiscent of mammalian melanopsin. We combined expression mapping, behavioral assays, and phylogenetic comparisons to investigate its function. RH7 detects temporal changes in luminance, guiding rapid behavioral responses, and regulating daily activity patterns. Flies lacking RH7 are less active during the dark phase, while strains with constitutively active RH7 show increased activity. Phylogenetic analyses suggest that RH7 is an ancient rhodopsin present across panarthropods, representing an intermediate between G protein–coupled receptors and specialized rhodopsins, highlighting a key step in the evolution of non-visual light perception. These findings show that RH7 functions as a melanopsin-like sensor, shaping behavior, and illuminating the origins of light detection.

articles.title: Directional gate-error asymmetry and universal selectivity bounds in non-unital open quantum systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clifford randomized benchmarking and average gate fidelity assign a single trajectory-independent decay rate to a noisy quantum gate at leading order in the dimensionless damping exposure \varepsilon = \gamma T, concealing state-dependent transition-error asymmetries in untwirled quantum circuits. While state-dependent amplitude-damping errors are well known in open quantum systems, a trajectory-level analytical framework that bounds directional transition selectivity across arbitrary pulse shapes and Markovian environments has been lacking. Using first-order toggling-frame perturbation theory for a two-level qubit coupled to a Markovian bath, we show that the antipodal survival-error slopes \chi_+ and \chi_- along any piecewise-continuous control path depend exclusively on its time-averaged Bloch vector m and transverse residence covariance matrix G, obeying the complete-positivity cofactor bound \beta(r) \le 1. On a standard polar \sqrt{X} gate, longitudinal T_1 relaxation induces a 12.23 : 1 directional survival-error split (\kappa_{T_1} = (3\pi - 8)/(3\pi + 8) \approx 0.081767), whereas time-symmetric X rotations maintain an exact 1 : 1 balance (\kappa_{T_1} = 1). Across all completely positive Markovian generators, coupling between non-unital drift and unital diffusion enforces a selectivity bound \kappa_\star = (\pi - 2\sqrt{2})/(\pi + 2\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.052456 (19.06 : 1) for time-independent single-qubit \pi swaps. We apply this framework to Gaussian and derivative-removal-by-adiabatic-gate (DRAG) waveforms on superc

articles.title: Quantum Transitions From Integrable to Chaotic
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum integrable-to-chaotic transition is commonly pictured as the quantum counterpart of the classical Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) scenario: a phaseout transition in which a family of regular eigenstates coexists with, and gradually yields to, chaotic eigenstates. Here we show that this is not the only fundamental route from integrability to chaos in quantum systems. We identify a second elementary transition---the morphing transition---which has no classical counterpart: all eigenstates hybridize and turn chaotic concurrently, so that no regular subsequence survives at any stage of the crossover. The two transitions are spectrally distinct: the phaseout spectrum is an independent superposition of regular and chaotic subsequences with Berry-Robnik statistics and a finite short-spacing intercept $P(0)$, whereas the morphing spectrum exhibits global level repulsion with Lenz-Haake statistics and $P(0)=0$. We demonstrate both transitions, and their mixture, in three models. The results for the deformed boson model further show that the quantum phaseout scenario is conditional on a smooth quantum-classical correspondence.

articles.title: Optimal Frobenius light cones for power-law systems in any dimension
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove optimal Frobenius Lieb-Robinson bounds for power-law systems with power-law exponent $\alpha$ in any dimension $d$, in particular showing that the algebraic to linear light cone transition occurs at $\alpha=d+1$. The proof uses a spectral clipping method and concentration result to allow for running a multiscale operator-norm argument which produces the optimal Frobenius norm exponent. Additionally, we prove there is a Frobenius light cone transition from polylogarithmic to algebraic at the summability threshold $\alpha=d$, and a transition from decaying in volume to non-decaying in volume at $\alpha=d/2$.

articles.title: Metamorphic Testing of Quantum Software based on Stabilizer States
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A major challenge in quantum computing is to systematically check if a quantum program implements its desired functionality. For classical programs, testing is widely used; each test case comprises a pair of sample input and expected output to be compared with the actual output. To increase the number of test cases, however, one has to solve the test-oracle problem: for each additional test input one has to know the correct output. Metamorphic testing tackles this problem by utilizing metamorphic relations between input and output domains to automatically derive new test cases from existing ones. However, adapting metamorphic testing to the quantum realm is not straightforward, since quantum states cannot be directly inspected. We propose a framework of quantum metamorphic testing (QMT) in which the metamorphic relations incorporate the measurement procedures required to assess quantum outputs. We apply our QMT framework to testing the preparation of stabilizer states, which are central to protocols like measurement-based quantum computing or quantum error correction. We utilize structural properties of stabilizer states to systematically derive measurement circuits for new test cases from existing ones. We implement this framework in Qiskit, and demonstrate that it reduces by an order of magnitude the testing run time compared to testing with randomly generated input states. We further show effectiveness by revealing synthetic program faults injected by circuit mutations, as well as a real bug in the Qiskit compiler.

articles.title: Universal Quantum Computation in a Wigner's Friend Framework
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Wigner's Friend thought experiment illustrates a core tension in quantum mechanics: an observer inside an isolated laboratory (the Friend) measures a definite outcome, while an external observer (Wigner) describes the laboratory as a coherent superposition. Here we show that this discrepancy, usually studied as a conflict between descriptions, has a direct computational consequence. We namely propose a protocol by which Wigner can turn the Friend's laboratory into a universal quantum computer, whereby the Friend is restricted to apply simple classical operations within the laboratory. We also experimentally implement a proof-of-principle demonstration of this protocol for single-qubit gates using single photons. By recasting the coherence between incompatible descriptions as a computational resource, we thus link the foundations of quantum measurement to quantum computation.

articles.title: A Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem with Smooth Modulus
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for the vector dihedral coset problem over $\mathbb{Z}_q^n$, in which the goal is to recover $\mathbf{s} \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ given independent samples of the form $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\bigl(|{0,\mathbf{x}}\rangle+|{1,\mathbf{x}+\mathbf{s}}\rangle\bigr)$, for $\mathbf{x}\sim \mathbb{Z}_q^n$. When the modulus $q$ is $B$-smooth, the algorithm uses $n^{O(B^{1+o(1)}\log q)}B^{O(B^{2+o(1)}\log q)}$ samples and time. For $B = \mathrm{polylog}(n)$ and $q=\mathrm{poly}(n)$, this gives a quasipolynomial time- and sample-complexity. This extends the previously known quasipolynomial-time result for power-of-two moduli (Bonnetain, Naya-Plasencia, ASIACRYPT 2018; Bai, Jangir, Kirshanova, Ngo, Youmans, CRYPTO 2025). The algorithm proceeds by reducing the modulus one prime factor $p | q$ at a time. The key ingredient is a sieving procedure that clears the non-linear terms in the phase modulo $p$ via an algorithm of Ivanyos, Santha (TCS 2017) that finds non-zero $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{F}_p^\ell$ such that $\sum_{i \in [\ell]} u_i^d \mathbf{a}_i = 0 \mod p$ for degrees $1 \le d \le p-1$, given vectors $\mathbf{a}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_\ell \in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ as input. The algorithm also applies to the extrapolated dihedral coset problem (EDCP) introduced by Brakerski, Kirshanova, Stehl\'e, Wen (PKC 2018), which is known to be equivalent to LWE in the polynomial sample regime. However, our result does not yield a new attack on LWE in any regime, precisely because the known reduction from LWE to EDCP provides only poly

articles.title: Double-Randomized Quantum Singular Value Transformations For Early Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computers
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) is an algorithmic framework which encompasses a wide range of problems, including Hamiltonian dynamics, ground state preparation, Gibbs state preparation, amplitude amplification, and matrix inversion. For many areas of scientific interest such as quantum chemistry and condensed matter, the circuit depth of the block-encoding subroutine in QSVT can be formidable, limiting the scope of problems to which QSVT can be applied on early fault-tolerant hardware. We split linear operators $A$ into a core operator $A_0$ and a tail operator $A_\epsilon$, block-encoding the normalized sum of $A_0$ and the average of $n_T$ randomly sampled terms from $A_\epsilon$. We show that using randomized block-encodings of this form allows one to lower the circuit depth of QSVT while incurring a diamond norm error that scales as $\mathcal{O}(C_P\delta^2/n_T$), where $C_P$ is a prefactor which depends on the QSVT polynomial $P$ and $\delta$ is the ratio of the $\ell_1$ norms of the coefficient vectors of $A_\epsilon$ and $A$. We then go on to show that if one samples QSVT circuits from a joint probability distribution of both random block-encodings and random polynomials (Double-Randomized QSVT), then the circuit depth savings of these two randomization techniques combine multiplicatively, with only additive error contributions. We numerically calculate error bounds for long-range Heisenberg and iron-sulfur complex Hamiltonians, showing that for a diamond norm error bound of $10^{-3}$, RBE-QSVT can red

articles.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.

articles.title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a trained quantum generative model has learned its target is usually decided by a diagnostic validated on a labeled benchmark, and such a diagnostic can pass that validation by recovering how the benchmark was built. We analyze Fisher-trace and kernel-based certification of the real-amplitude quantum circuit Born machine in noiseless statevector simulation. For real-amplitude circuits built from half-angle rotations, the classical Fisher information equals the quantum Fisher information almost everywhere, so its trace equals the parameter count and carries no information about fit quality. The Fisher eigenvalue rank counts the live nodes of the amplitude tree: it coincides with the label on a sparse benchmark and is uninformative on a full-support one. The pooled Wasserstein and maximum-mean-discrepancy scores move with optimizer convergence and with the scoring convention. For two bitstring defect families on which both metrics have closed forms, we compute the tolerance-mismatch window in which the discrepancy rejects generators that the transport threshold admits; it opens only at certification-grade tolerances and closes as the qubit number grows. On the Hamming cost we prove a sharp tolerance ratio above which the discrepancy vote is redundant, and we obtain the exact worst-parity minimax value over all unit-diagonal positive-semidefinite kernels, which is exponentially small in the qubit number. In a numerical campaign at the tolerances a near-term experiment can resolve, the discrepancy vote changed no verdict a

articles.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

articles.title: Quantum Coloring Games on Complete Graphs
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonlocal game where two players are both given an input ($x$ and $y$, respectively), from a set of size $n$ and, without communicating, must give outputs $a$ and $b$, respectively, from a set of size $m < n$, winning when $(x = y) \leftrightarrow (a = b)$. This can be considered a graph coloring game on the complete graph with $n$ vertices. In the simplest case, the players get random equal inputs with probability $\frac{1}{2}$ and random unequal inputs otherwise. We solve this case of the game, and many others, for both classical and quantum (i.e., where the players may share finite-dimensional entangled quantum states) strategy sets, proving the value (the probability of winning) of the optimal strategies and providing explicit strategies that attain this optimum for all $n$ and $m$. Our optimal strategies are synchronous: i.e., the two players always give equal outputs when given equal inputs. These strategies remain optimal when the probability of receiving equal inputs is at least $\frac{2}{m + 2}$. Across this wide range of cases, we find that quantum strategies have an advantage over classical strategies exactly when $m$ does not divide $n$; this advantage is $O\left(\frac{m}{n^2}\right)$.

articles.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cram\'er-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.

articles.title: Control of Non-Markovianity via Channel Exceptional Points in a Driven-Dissipative Kerr-Cat Qubit
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in open quantum systems are conventionally defined at the Liouvillian level, making them representation-dependent and often requiring auxiliary degrees of freedom. We study EPs directly at the quantum-channel level in a driven-dissipative Kerr-cat qubit, in which dissipation drives bidirectional jumps between its two basis states. Interpolating two Markovian channels yields single EPs when the endpoints straddle a spectral-phase boundary and, remarkably, double EPs within the same phase. The interpolated EPs map out a Markovian--non-Markovian phase diagram: the parameter plane separates certified non-Markovian and Markovian domains, with domain boundaries switching the channel between the two characters. Three spectral criteria certify every domain. As the evolution time advances, the domains drift, split, and partially shrink, making the switching increasingly sensitive to parameters and time. This establishes a representation-independent paradigm for classifying and switching quantum memory effects, applicable to continuous-variable, discrete-variable, and hybrid systems.

articles.title: Machine-learned active spaces enable quantum calculations of spin-state energetics of transition-metal complexes on quantum hardware
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multireference calculations on transition-metal complexes, on classical or quantum hardware, depend on the choice of active space. The orbitals that belong in it are those that are strongly entangled in the correlated wavefunction, but measuring this entanglement requires the very correlated calculation that the active space is meant to make affordable. Here we present SpinAware, a machine-learning model that predicts density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) single-orbital entropies and orbital-pair mutual information from the unrestricted Hartree-Fock (UHF) solution of each spin state, without any correlated calculation. Each of the 20 highest occupied and 20 lowest unoccupied orbitals is described by 60 descriptors computed from the UHF solution, among them the differences between its alpha and beta occupations and energies, its metal-d and ligand character, and its exchange coupling to the other orbitals, and a transformer predicts the entropy of each orbital in the context of all others. Trained on 3454 spin-pure DMRG calculations on mononuclear Cr-Ni complexes, the model transfers to experimentally characterized complexes with ligands, binding topologies, oxidation states and metals absent from training. Over 11 spin states it reproduces the DMRG entropy profiles with a mean absolute error of 0.027, and combining the predicted entropies with the predicted mutual information gives a candidate pool that contains 99% of the DMRG-active orbitals of the benchmark spin states while keeping, on average, only 15 of the 40 orbi

articles.title: Constrained Adiabatic Quantum Programming
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To find a $k$-clique in a graph, adiabatic quantum computation (AQC) evolves a quantum system from the minimum of an initial cost function to the minimum of a problem cost function that penalizes non-cliques. Existing AQC languages fix the initial cost function, so the search ranges over all $2^n$ subsets of the $n$ vertices, although only the subsets of size $k$ can be answers. We present ENQ+, an AQC language in which the programmer writes both cost functions. Data constraints define the problem cost function. Relational constraints, a new construct, declare the moves the search may make between configurations and define the initial cost function. For the clique, a single relational constraint, which exchanges a chosen vertex with an unchosen one, confines the search to the subsets of size $k$. ENQ+ thereby turns constrained quantum annealing, which physicists set up by hand for individual problems, into a programming construct. We give ENQ+ a semantics in many-world configuration (MWC) graphs, whose nodes are configurations and whose edges are moves, and derive from it a step-wise semantics of adiabatic evolution. We prove that a run stays within the component of the MWC graph that contains its initial state, and that a run from an approximate initial state still reaches the answer, with probability equal to its squared overlap with the exact one. We compile ENQ+ to quantum circuits, prove the compilation correct with respect to the semantics, and use ENQ+ to program the Three-Dimensional Matching, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Tr

articles.title: Efficient simulation of the generalized Langevin equation using a basis of dynamically relevant histories for memory and noise
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Generalized Langevin Equation (GLE) is a cornerstone for modeling non-Markovian dynamics, but its numerical solution remains challenging due to the history-dependent convolution and the need to generate colored noise with a prescribed correlation function. We introduce a forward construction that addresses both challenges within a single framework. We represent an arbitrary trajectory as sum of relevant and irrelevant parts, where relevant part can be decomposed into a small number of characteristic history patterns that make the main contribution to future dynamics. It allows to reduce numerical cost to \(O(d^2)\) for $d$ chosen patterns instead of full history. The same construction applies to colored noise generation, where the causal filter plays the role of the memory kernel. We demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method for several representative kernels, including long-range kernels with power-law tails.

articles.title: Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. Guided by these dynamical signatures, SCOPE explores multiple perturbed decoding trajectories in parallel, enabling early termination and reseeding within a fixed serial iteration budget, with message-passing parameters optimized offline by simulated annealing. Circuit-level simulations of the $[[144,12,12]]$ BB code yield a logical error rate of $p_L=4.82\times10^{-10}$ at a physical error rate of $p=10^{-3}$. We further realize a pipelined two-arm memory-augmented BP (Mem-BP) core at the register-transfer level. Functional simulations at a 250 MHz clock yield a 16 ns BP iteration interval per arm and a mean input-to-result latency of 173.8 ns at $p=5\times10^{-3}$.

articles.title: Excitation-Selective Control of Protected Subradiant Antiresonances
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Subradiant cavity antiresonances exhibit narrow spectral features, yet controlling their nonlinear response without perturbing the protected resonance remains challenging. Here we demonstrate excitation-selective control of a subradiant antiresonance in a driven two-emitter cavity-QED system. An auxiliary collective channel leaves the antisymmetric single-excitation state unaffected while shifting the doubly excited state, introducing tunable excitation anharmonicity without altering the linear antiresonance. This separation enables control of two-photon excitation pathways and photon correlations. Independently, a spatial coupling phase tunes optical access to the subradiant state without changing its intrinsic decay rate. We find that the interferometric phase information per incident photon is optimized when cavity-induced readout approximately matches intrinsic subradiant decay, while steady-state atomic entanglement peaks at an intermediate coupling phase. We further extend phase-selective optical control to collective subradiant modes in correlated emitter arrays. These results establish collective symmetry and spatial mode matching as distinct controls of nonlinear photon correlations, optical phase information, and atomic entanglement.

articles.title: Scalable and Interpretable Quantum Mixture of Experts for High-Dimensional Spatio-Temporal Data
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Mixture of Experts (QMoE) architectures offer a promising path toward scalable quantum machine learning, yet existing approaches remain largely confined to low-dimensional benchmarks and often rely on naive input partitioning that disrupts feature dependencies. We address these gaps by introducing Feature-Partitioned QMoE, which partitions high-dimensional spatio-temporal inputs into functionally coherent feature groups and assigns each group to a dedicated quantum expert. We further propose a hierarchical interpretability framework that leverages the modular structure of QMoE to produce circuit-level gating analysis, per-expert gradient saliency, and heterogeneity-based subtype discovery. Applied to ADHD classification from resting-state fMRI (N=4,458, ABCD Study, 180 brain ROIs, 363 timepoints), the proposed Theory-Driven QMoE achieves performance comparable to matched-capacity classical and quantum baselines while enabling circuit-attributable interpretation. The framework identifies FDR-corrected ADHD-associated biomarkers in executive-control and anterior default-mode networks and reveals three neurobiologically meaningful ADHD subtypes. These results position Feature-Partitioned QMoE as a scalable and interpretable methodology for applying quantum machine learning to high-dimensional biomedical data.

articles.title: Advancing Quantum Reinforcement Learning with Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search and Adaptive Non-local Observables
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.19182v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ans\"atze. Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) address these issues independently, but to our knowledge have not been combined or compared in a single QRL framework. We present an ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the Quantum Time-series Transformer (QTSTransformer), evaluated on a 2 x 2 factorial design across six environments--two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games. Three findings emerge. First, the quantum agent outperforms a matched classical transformer baseline on five of six environments, with absolute scores ranging from 360.0 vs 304.0 (MarioBros) to 17.2 vs 2.5 (Breakout), while using approximately 12.5x fewer transformer parameters on the four Atari environments (more modestly so on the two classic-control tasks). Second, ANO and DiffQAS provide complementary benefits: ANO yields the largest gain on continuous-state CartPole (347.7 vs 223.2), while DiffQAS yields the largest absolute Atari gains (Breakout 17.2 vs 3.0; DonkeyKong 70.0 vs 37.0). Third, combining both innovations exhibits an asymmetric interaction: ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS, whereas DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade when ANO is added. These results provide design guidance for QRL agents: select between ANO and DiffQAS according to whether the bottleneck is the measurement basis or the gate topology, rather than applying both in

articles.title: Adaptation of an herbivorous arthropod to green tea plants by overcoming catechin defenses
articles.summary: Green tea catechins protect tea plants from biotic stressors. Among herbivorous mites, the generalist Tetranychus urticae has not been reported as a tea pest. In contrast, some populations of Tetranychus kanzawai thrive on tea plants. Here, we investigated the mechanism of this adaptation. Green tea catechins were repellent and toxic to T. urticae and tea non-adapted T. kanzawai and had an antifeedant effect on the latter. We identified an intradiol ring-cleavage dioxygenase DOG15, a gene horizontally transferred from fungi, as required for the adaptation of T. kanzawai to tea plants. Tea feeding strongly induces DOG15 expression in tea-adapted T. kanzawai, with mRNA and protein levels up to 31.6 and 12.1 times higher than in tea-fed T. urticae. We also identified two amino acid substitutions in DOG15 between the two Tetranychus species that increased the catechin-cleaving activity of the T. kanzawai enzyme. These substitutions predispose T. kanzawai but not T. urticae for the adaptation to tea plants. Inducible expression of modified DOG15 then enables T. kanzawai to efficiently detoxify green tea catechins. Our findings reveal how a horizontally transferred gene can be co-opted through structural and regulatory changes to overcome plant chemical defenses.

articles.title: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in the Drosophila brain
articles.summary: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE–gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE–gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE–gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE–gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE–gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity

articles.title: Hierarchical neural circuit theory of normalization and inter-areal communication
articles.summary: The primate brain exhibits a hierarchical, modular architecture with conserved microcircuits executing canonical computations across reciprocally connected cortical areas. We present a hierarchical neural circuit theory with feedback connections that dynamically implements divisive normalization across its hierarchy. In a two-stage instantiation (V1 ↔ V2), increasing feedback from V2 to V1 amplifies responses in both areas. We analytically derive power spectra (V1) and coherence spectra (V1-V2) as functions of frequency (f) and compare them with experimental observations: peaks in both spectra shift to higher frequencies with increased stimulus contrast, and power decays as 1/f4 at high frequencies. The closed-form spectra are validated against direct stochastic simulation of the full nonlinear circuit across contrasts. The theory further predicts distinctive spectral signatures of feedback and input gain modulation. Crucially, the theory offers a unified view of inter-areal communication, defined as the ability to linearly predict neural activity in one brain area from neural activity in another, with emergent features consistent with empirical observations of both communication subspaces and inter-areal coherence. It admits a low-dimensional communication subspace, where inter-areal communication is lower-dimensional than within-area communication. It further predicts that: (1) increasing feedback strength enhances inter-areal communication and diminishes within-area communication, without altering the subspace dimensionality; (2) communication is

articles.title: WNK-SPAK/OSR1 signaling pathway facilitates ictal activity via reduced neuronal chloride extrusion rate
articles.summary: Seizures upregulate Na<sup>+</sup>-K<sup>+</sup>–2Cl<sup>−</sup> (NKCC1)-mediated Cl<sup>−</sup> influx and downregulate K<sup>+</sup>-Cl<sup>−</sup> (KCC2)-mediated Cl<sup>−</sup> efflux via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 kinases, leading to cytoplasmic chloride ([Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub>) accumulation, reduced GABAergic inhibition, and anticonvulsant failure. Early studies found that inhibiting WNK-kinase reduced baseline [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> (E<sub>Cl</sub>) and seizures via increased KCC2 activity. However, increased KCC2 activity alone should not affect E<sub>Cl</sub>, whose determinants are more complex. We determined the net effects of the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway inhibitor WNK463 on E<sub>Cl</sub> and [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> transients during spontaneous ictal-like discharges (ILDs) in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures from mice. We found that WNK463 reduced interictal [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub>, but did not change baseline [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> measured in the presence of TTX. WNK463 enhanced neuronal Cl<sup>−</sup> extrusion during and after ILDs before abolishing ILDs. Pharmacological inhibition and targeted siRNA silencing demonstrated that the anti-ictal effects of WNK463 involved both NKCC1 and KCC2. Our data support a mechanism whereby mutual NKCC1 inhibition and KCC2 activation via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway exert powerful anti-ictal effects by facilitating [Cl<sup>−</sup>]<sub>i</sub> extrusion during ILDs.

articles.title: Correction: Deciphering the preeclampsia-specific immune microenvironment and the role of pro-inflammatory macrophages at the maternal–fetal interface
ITK deficiency protects against autoimmune pulmonary hemorrhage in mice by promoting amphiregulin-producing regulatory T cells
articles.summary: Pulmonary hemorrhage (PH) is a life-threatening manifestation of systemic autoimmunity caused by immune-mediated disruption of the alveolar capillary barrier. Despite high mortality, the molecular checkpoints that shift destructive inflammation toward protective immune regulation remain poorly defined. Here, using a pristane-induced PH mouse model, we identify interleukin-2-inducible T-cell kinase (ITK) as a critical regulator of autoimmune lung injury. ITK deficiency (Itk⁻/⁻) conferred near-complete protection from PH and associated multiorgan injury, accompanied by reduced proinflammatory monocytes and neutrophils and increased Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs). Adoptive transfer of Itk⁻/⁻ Tregs protected wild-type recipients from PH and suppressed systemic proinflammatory cytokines, identifying Tregs as key mediators of tissue protection. Mechanistically, lung Itk⁻/⁻ Tregs exhibited increased amphiregulin, a mediator of tissue repair. Transcriptomic profiling further showed that ITK loss reprogrammed Tregs toward a metabolically and functionally enhanced state, with enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation, mTORC1, and STAT5 signaling, and tissue-repair programs. These findings establish ITK as a regulator of the balance between pulmonary injury and reparative immunity and support targeting the ITK axis in severe inflammatory lung disease.
